note: Measures the bodies vote on. Dates are the record's unless marked; every effect is GAMEPLAY TUNING and invented. A measure of a dispatch body is a request sent to London: it is voted on when it arrives and its effect lands when the answer comes back. Contract: protocol/schemas/politics.yaml.

measures.title: Raise the army
measures.text: Resolve that an army of 30,000 men be raised at once, 13,600 of them by this colony.

passed.summary: Six units of militia enlist at Cambridge.

failed.summary: The towns keep their men at home: Support -3.

measures.note: The Provincial Congress resolved on 23 April 1775 that an army of 30,000 be raised, Massachusetts to furnish 13,600.

measures.title: Call on the neighbouring colonies
measures.text: Write to New Hampshire, Rhode Island and Connecticut for their share of the army.

passed.summary: Four units from the other New England colonies join at Cambridge. They go home if Unity falls too low.

failed.summary: No help is asked for: army morale -3.

measures.note: With the resolve of 23 April the Provincial Congress applied to the other New England colonies for their quotas; their troops reached the siege in the following weeks. The day of the vote is the game's.

measures.title: Enlist the Stockbridge company
measures.text: Take the Stockbridge Mohican minute men into service on their own terms, and send each man who enlists a blanket and a ribbon.

passed.summary: -12 gold for blankets and ribbons. The Stockbridge Company comes to Cambridge under its own captain: it is never merged into another army, and it goes home if it is left unpaid or Unity falls too low.

terms.text: The Provincial Congress voted 23 pounds for blankets and ribbons to be given to the Stockbridge men who enlisted.
Their sachem Solomon Uhhaunauwaunmut answered the Congress on 11 April 1775; the company served at the siege under its own officers, with Captain William Goodrich.
12 gold for the gift, two units for the company, and its leaving when unpaid or when Unity is low.

measures.note: Stockbridge Mohican men enlisted as minute men and served at the siege of Boston, some of them at Bunker Hill. The day of the vote is the game's.

measures.title: Adopt the army before Boston
measures.text: Take the New England army into the pay and service of the United Colonies.

passed.summary: Congress pays 40 in every 100 of the army's pay.

failed.summary: The army stays a New England charge: New England cools.

measures.note: Congress voted on 14 June 1775 to raise companies in its own pay and took the army before Boston as its own.

measures.title: Raise the rifle companies
measures.text: Ten companies of expert riflemen from Pennsylvania, Maryland and Virginia, to march to Boston.

passed.summary: The companies are raised; they will take seven weeks on the road.

effects.summary: The rifle companies march in: three units of riflemen at Cambridge.

measures.note: Voted on 14 June 1775; the first companies reached Cambridge at the end of July and in early August.

measures.title: Name a commander in chief
measures.text: A general to command all the continental forces: Colonel Washington of Virginia is proposed.

passed.summary: Washington is named: the Southern colonies warm. He will be seventeen days on the road.

effects.summary: General Washington reaches Cambridge: he may be given an army. Army morale +4.

failed.summary: No commander is named: the Southern colonies cool.

measures.note: Congress chose Washington on 15 June 1775; he reached Cambridge on 2 July and took command the next day.

measures.title: Emit bills of credit
measures.text: Two million Spanish dollars in paper, for the defence of America.

passed.summary: +120 gold now. Prices will rise as the paper spreads.

effects.summary: The paper money has spread: everything bought costs a quarter more.

measures.note: Congress resolved on 22 June 1775 to emit bills of credit to two million dollars. Continental paper lost value as more was printed.

measures.title: The Olive Branch Petition
measures.text: A last humble petition to the King, asking him to stop the war and find a way to be reconciled.

passed.summary: The British envoy's Attitude +10. New England cools; the Middle colonies warm.

failed.summary: No petition is sent: the Middle colonies cool.

measures.note: Adopted by Congress on 5 July 1775 and signed on 8 July. The King refused to receive it.

measures.title: A committee to import powder
measures.text: A secret committee to contract for gunpowder and arms from abroad.

passed.summary: 3 powder a month come in to the Cambridge magazine.

failed.summary: The army goes on begging powder town by town.

measures.note: Congress appointed the Secret Committee on 18 September 1775 to contract for the importation of gunpowder.

measures.title: Fit out armed vessels
measures.text: Two swift vessels to cruise against the transports that bring the enemy his stores.

passed.summary: Prizes come in: 2 muskets and 1 powder a month at Cambridge.

measures.note: Congress voted on 13 October 1775 to fit out two armed vessels to intercept British supply ships.

measures.title: Reinforcement with three generals
measures.text: More regiments for Boston, and Major Generals Howe, Clinton and Burgoyne to serve under the commander in chief.

passed.summary: Eight units land at Boston with Generals Howe, Clinton and Burgoyne.

measures.note: The Cerberus brought Howe, Clinton and Burgoyne into Boston on 25 May 1775; more regiments followed that summer. It was ordered before the campaign opens, so it is already at sea. The number of units is the game's.

measures.title: A provision convoy
measures.text: Salt meat, flour and coal for the garrison, under escort.

failed.summary: The Treasury will not pay for the convoy.

measures.note: The garrison of Boston was fed from Britain and Ireland by sea throughout the siege. The dates and the amount are the game's.

measures.title: Proclaim martial law
measures.text: Martial law in Massachusetts, and pardon to all who lay down their arms, Samuel Adams and John Hancock excepted.

passed.summary: The garrison's morale +3. Patriot Support +2: the country takes it as a threat.

measures.note: Gage, who had been ordered from London to proclaim martial law, issued his proclamation on 12 June 1775, offering pardon to all but Samuel Adams and John Hancock.

measures.title: Proclaim the colonies in rebellion
measures.text: A royal proclamation for suppressing rebellion and sedition.

passed.summary: The envoy's Attitude -15: he may no longer treat rebels gently. The ministry's confidence +5. Patriot Support +3.

measures.note: George III proclaimed the colonies in open rebellion on 23 August 1775. That is the date it was issued in London; applying it at Boston the same day is the game's.

measures.title: Reprisals on the coast
measures.text: Leave for the squadron to lay waste the seaport towns that have armed against the King, and to take what supplies they hold.

passed.summary: 20 provisions are brought in to Boston. Patriot Support +5: the burnt towns turn the coast against the King.

failed.summary: The squadron keeps to its blockade.

measures.note: On Admiral Graves's orders of 6 October 1775 a squadron burned Falmouth (now Portland, Maine) on 18 October.

measures.title: Leave to evacuate Boston
measures.text: Discretion for the commander to quit Boston and carry the army to a better station.

passed.summary: The commander at Boston may sail when he judges it right.

measures.note: The ministers wrote in the autumn of 1775 that the army might leave Boston; the army sailed for Halifax on 17 March 1776. The day the leave arrives here is the game's.
